type shape =
  | Circle({radius: float})
  | Rect({width: float, height: float})
  | Point

type user = {
  name: string,
  @Json.key("user_age") age: int,
  email: option<string>,
  tags: array<string>,
  avatar: shape,
}

let alice = {
  name: "Alice",
  age: 30,
  email: None,
  tags: ["admin", "staff"],
  avatar: Circle({radius: 2.5}),
}

let rec encode$user = (a$: user): JSON.t =>
  JSON.Encode.object(
    Dict.fromArray([
      ("name", encode$string(a$.name)),
      ("user_age", encode$int(a$.age)),
      ("email", encode$option_string(a$.email)),
      ("tags", encode$array_string(a$.tags)),
      ("avatar", encode$shape(a$.avatar)),
    ]),
  )
and encode$shape = (a$: shape): JSON.t =>
  switch a$ {
  | Circle({radius: radius$0}) =>
    JSON.Encode.object(
      Dict.fromArray([
        ("tag", JSON.Encode.string("Circle")),
        ("radius", encode$float(radius$0)),
      ]),
    )
  | Rect({width: width$0, height: height$1}) =>
    JSON.Encode.object(
      Dict.fromArray([
        ("tag", JSON.Encode.string("Rect")),
        ("width", encode$float(width$0)),
        ("height", encode$float(height$1)),
      ]),
    )
  | Point => JSON.Encode.object(Dict.fromArray([("tag", JSON.Encode.string("Point"))]))
  }
and encode$string = (a$: string): JSON.t => JSON.Encode.string(a$)
and encode$int = (a$: int): JSON.t => JSON.Encode.int(a$)
and encode$option_string = (a$: option<string>): JSON.t =>
  switch a$ {
  | Some(v) => encode$string(v)
  | None => JSON.Encode.null
  }
and encode$array_string = (a$: array<string>): JSON.t =>
  JSON.Encode.array(a$->Array.map(v => encode$string(v)))
and encode$float = (a$: float): JSON.t => JSON.Encode.float(a$)

Console.log(JSON.stringify(encode$user(alice), ~space=2))

// The type can come from inference: nothing in the callback says `user`.
let team = [alice, {...alice, name: "Bob", avatar: Point}]

Console.log(team->Array.map(member => JSON.stringify(encode$shape(member.avatar))))

type color =
  | Red
  | Green
  | @Enum.label("navy blue") Blue

let colorToString = (value: color): string =>
  switch value {
  | Red => "Red"
  | Green => "Green"
  | Blue => "navy blue"
  }
let colorFromString = (text: string): option<color> =>
  switch text {
  | "Red" => Some(Red)
  | "Green" => Some(Green)
  | "navy blue" => Some(Blue)
  | _ => None
  }
let colorValues: array<color> = [Red, Green, Blue]

Console.log(colorValues->Array.map(colorToString))
Console.log(colorFromString("navy blue") == Some(Blue))
Console.log(colorFromString("purple"))

open Macro

let capitalize = (text: string) =>
  String.toUpperCase(String.charAt(text, 0)) ++ String.slice(text, ~start=1)

// A macro can return any number of declarations: here two conversion
// functions per unit. Used as `module Length = %Units.table(...)`.
@macro
let table = (base: string, units: array<(string, float)>): decls =>
  Code.decls(
    units->Array.map(((unit, factor)) =>
      Macro.__quoteDecls(
        [
          [("\n        let ", 12, 12)],
          [(" = (value: float) => value *. ", 13, 56)],
          [("\n        let ", 13, 107)],
          [(" = (value: float) => value /. ", 14, 56)],
          [("\n      ", 14, 107)],
        ],
        [
          Macro.__holePat(Pat.var(unit ++ "To" ++ capitalize(base))),
          Macro.__holeCode(Code.float(factor)),
          Macro.__holePat(Pat.var(base ++ "To" ++ capitalize(unit))),
          Macro.__holeCode(Code.float(factor)),
        ],
        "Units.res",
      )
    ),
  )

open Macro

exception DecodeError(string)
let fail = (message: string) => throw(DecodeError(message))

let field = (json: JSON.t, key: string): JSON.t =>
  switch json {
  | Object(fields) => fields->Dict.get(key)->Option.getOr(JSON.Null)
  | _ => fail(`expected an object with the field "${key}"`)
  }

// The result type of this @generic is a type variable: nothing in the
// arguments says what to decode to. `expected()` is the type the call site
// wants, so the annotation `let user: user = ...` picks the decoder.
@generic
let fromJson = (json: code<JSON.t>): code<'a> =>
  switch Type.info(expected()) {
  | String =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("\n      switch ", 19, 10)],
        [
          (" {\n      | String(text) => text\n      | _ => ", 20, 20),
          ("Decode.", 0, 0),
          ("fail(\"expected a string\")\n      }\n    ", 22, 13),
        ],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(json)],
      "Decode.res",
    )
  | Int =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("\n      switch ", 26, 10)],
        [
          (" {\n      | Number(number) => Float.toInt(number)\n      | _ => ", 27, 20),
          ("Decode.", 0, 0),
          ("fail(\"expected a number\")\n      }\n    ", 29, 13),
        ],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(json)],
      "Decode.res",
    )
  | Bool =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("\n      switch ", 33, 10)],
        [
          (" {\n      | Boolean(bool) => bool\n      | _ => ", 34, 20),
          ("Decode.", 0, 0),
          ("fail(\"expected true or false\")\n      }\n    ", 36, 13),
        ],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(json)],
      "Decode.res",
    )
  | Option(inner) =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("\n      switch ", 40, 10)],
        [
          (" {\n      | Null => None\n      | present => Some((", 41, 20),
          ("Decode.", 0, 0),
          ("fromJson(present): ", 43, 25),
        ],
        [("))\n      }\n    ", 43, 52)],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(json), Macro.__holeType(inner)],
      "Decode.res",
    )
  | Array(inner) =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("\n      switch ", 47, 10)],
        [
          (" {\n      | Array(items) => items->Array.map(item => (", 48, 20),
          ("Decode.", 0, 0),
          ("fromJson(item): ", 49, 50),
        ],
        [
          ("))\n      | _ => ", 49, 74),
          ("Decode.", 0, 0),
          ("fail(\"expected an array\")\n      }\n    ", 50, 13),
        ],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(json), Macro.__holeType(inner)],
      "Decode.res",
    )
  | Record({fields}) =>
    // `entryOf` writes `name: value`, and `name: ?value` for an optional
    // field: its type is an option, and a key that is missing leaves it out.
    Code.record(
      fields->Array.map(f =>
        Code.entryOf(
          f,
          Macro.__quoteCode(
            [
              [
                ("(", 58, 30),
                ("Decode.", 0, 0),
                ("fromJson(", 58, 31),
                ("Decode.", 0, 0),
                ("field(", 58, 40),
              ],
              [(", ", 58, 53)],
              [(")): ", 58, 79)],
              [(")", 58, 91)],
            ],
            [
              Macro.__holeCode(json),
              Macro.__holeCode(Code.string(f.jsName)),
              Macro.__holeType(f.typ),
            ],
            "Decode.res",
          ),
        )
      ),
    )
  | _ => error(`Decode.fromJson cannot decode to ${Type.name(expected())}`)
  }

open Macro

// Two arguments of the same type. The comparison is written out per type:
// no run-time reflection, no walking of unknown values.
@generic
let equal = (a: code<'a>, b: code<'a>): code<bool> =>
  switch Type.info(typeOf(a)) {
  | Int | Float | String | Bool | Unit | BigInt | Char =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [[], [(" === ", 8, 68)], []],
      [Macro.__holeCode(a), Macro.__holeCode(b)],
      "Equal.res",
    )
  | Option(_) =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("\n      switch (", 10, 10)],
        [(", ", 11, 18)],
        [
          (") {\n      | (Some(left), Some(right)) => ", 11, 24),
          ("Equal.", 0, 0),
          (
            "equal(left, right)\n      | (None, None) => true\n      | _ => false\n      }\n    ",
            12,
            37,
          ),
        ],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(a), Macro.__holeCode(b)],
      "Equal.res",
    )
  | Array(_) =>
    Macro.__quoteCode(
      [
        [("{\n      let (left, right) = (", 18, 10)],
        [(", ", 19, 31)],
        [
          (
            ")\n      Array.length(left) == Array.length(right) &&\n        left->Array.everyWithIndex((item, index) => ",
            19,
            37,
          ),
          ("Equal.", 0, 0),
          ("equal(item, right->Array.getUnsafe(index)))\n    }", 21, 52),
        ],
      ],
      [Macro.__holeCode(a), Macro.__holeCode(b)],
      "Equal.res",
    )
  | Record({fields}) =>
    fields->Array.reduce(Macro.__quoteCode([[("true", 24, 31)]], [], "Equal.res"), (all, f) =>
      Macro.__quoteCode(
        [
          [],
          [(" && ", 25, 18), ("Equal.", 0, 0), ("equal(", 25, 22)],
          [(", ", 25, 52)],
          [(")", 25, 78)],
        ],
        [
          Macro.__holeCode(all),
          Macro.__holeCode(a->Code.field(f.name)),
          Macro.__holeCode(b->Code.field(f.name)),
        ],
        "Equal.res",
      )
    )
  | _ => error(`Equal.equal cannot compare values of type ${Type.name(typeOf(a))}`)
  }

type theme = Light | Dark | Custom(string)

type settings = {
  name: string,
  retries: int,
  verbose: bool,
  tags: array<string>,
  theme: theme,
  proxy: option<string>,
}

let rec value$settings = (_: unit): settings => {
  name: value$string(),
  retries: value$int(),
  verbose: value$bool(),
  tags: value$array_string(),
  theme: value$theme(),
  proxy: value$option_string(),
}
and value$string = (_: unit): string => ""
and value$int = (_: unit): int => 0
and value$bool = (_: unit): bool => false
and value$array_string = (_: unit): array<string> => []
and value$theme = (_: unit): theme => Light
and value$option_string = (_: unit): option<string> => None

let initial: settings = value$settings()

Console.log(initial)
Console.log({...initial, name: "production", retries: 3})
